heroHeadline: 19 Days to Kickoff — Pochettino Names USMNT 26-Man Squad with Pulisic Leading Host Nation
heroSubtitle: England head coach Thomas Tuchel named his final 26-player World Cup squad at Wembley on May 22 — the defining omissions being Cole Palmer (Chelsea), Phil Foden (Man City), Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), and Harry Maguire, who called the snub 'shocking and gutting.' Harry Kane captains for a record-tying third World Cup (equalling Billy Wright); Jordan Henderson makes a record-tying fourth appearance matching Sir Bobby Charlton; Ivan Toney (Al-Ahli) is the surprise recall; nine debutants are included. England open Group L vs Croatia. Tuchel's stated ambition: 'We have 26 one-hundred per cent committed players — the goal is to try and win it.' A new crisis emerged May 22: DR Congo cancelled their planned Kinshasa pre-tournament farewell training camp after a Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak (130+ confirmed dead, ~600 suspected cases) was declared a WHO public health emergency; the US CDC imposed a 21-day entry ban on travelers from Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan — directly threatening any DR Congo delegation member who returned home after early May. White House Task Force Director Andrew Giuliani said DR Congo must 'maintain the integrity of their bubble for 21 days before they can come to Houston.' Congo's squad (training in Belgium) is currently unaffected but the logistics represent a major new risk alongside the Iran visa situation. USMNT injury alert: Chris Richards (2025 US Soccer Male Player of the Year) tore two ankle ligaments and is rated 50/50 for Pochettino's May 26 NYC roster announcement. Iran: still no US visas approved despite squad applying at Ankara embassy on May 21; warm-up vs Gambia in Antalya on May 29. Spain squad announcement: May 25 (De La Fuente — Lamine Yamal fitness uncertain). Final rosters due June 1; FIFA publishes all 48 squads June 2.
